claim: Twitch paid out $889 million to streamers in January-September 2021, up 71% from $519 million in the same nine months of 2020, with September 2021 alone totalling $102 million.
stance_target: Aggregate creator payouts on Twitch grew rapidly even as per-creator income remained negligible for most
scope_conditions: Derived from the leaked internal payout records, so this is measured platform telemetry rather than survey; direct Twitch payouts only; monthly series shows no cyclicality
quoted_support: Its most recent data point, September 2021, shows a total monthly payout of $102 million, up +42 percent from $71 million a year ago, and +179 percent from $37 million in September 2019. For the period January through September, Twitch paid out $519 million last year compared to $889 million (+71%) in 2021.

claim: Twitch streamers derive approximately 56% of platform revenue from subscriptions, 20% from Prime subscriptions, and only about 9% from advertising.
stance_target: Audience volume strategies are structurally low-yield for creators; income depends on converting a small engaged core rather than on reach
scope_conditions: Averages across the leaked payout data, Aug 2019 - Oct 2021; Twitch-native revenue only; Prime subscriptions are free to the viewer, so 20% of streamer revenue derives from a channel viewers do not pay for directly
quoted_support: streamers receive only around 9% of their total income from ads ... subscriptions account for 56% of revenues ... Another 20% comes from Prime subscriptions but, in fairness, those are free to the viewer.

claim: Twitch's highest-earning channel generated $9,874 per on-air broadcast hour while the top 10 channels averaged $1,209 per on-air hour, and these rates exclude substantial unpaid off-camera labour.
stance_target: Top-tail creator earnings represent extraordinary hourly compensation
scope_conditions: CriticalRole earned $9.6m across 975 broadcast hours July 2019 - September 2021, hours measured by StreamHatchet (author discloses he is a StreamHatchet advisor); CriticalRole's revenue is split across a 30-plus person production company; on-air hours only
quoted_support: To earn its $9.6 million for the period July 2019 through September 2021, CriticalRole was on-air for a total of 975 hours. ... Among the top 10, the average number of dollars generated over the entire period per on-air hour is $1,209.

claim: Twitch had 8.1 million active streamers in September 2021, a figure that differs from the 8.8 million, 9 million, 7 million and 4.9 million denominators used by other analyses of the same leak.
stance_target: Percentage claims derived from the Twitch leak are comparable across outlets
scope_conditions: Denominator instability: 8.1m (van Dreunen, Sept 2021), 8.8m (Twitch Tracker via PC Gamer), 9m (Washington Post), 7m monthly live (Twitch's own 2023 disclosure), 4.9m accounts (leak-based percentile analyses), 2.4m streamers with payouts (Reuters via Wikipedia)
quoted_support: With 8.1 million active streamers on Twitch in September, it is impossibly difficult to stand out.

claim: A peer-reviewed study based on 100 streamer interviews conducted over two years identifies four categories of unpaid off-camera labour — marketing and social-media management, developing a unique visual style, networking inside other creators' streams, and administration — that make nominal hourly earnings a substantial overstatement of true compensation.
stance_target: Creator income per hour of total work is far lower than income per broadcast hour, which bears on burnout-driven attrition
scope_conditions: Mark Johnson, 'Behind the Streams: The Off-Camera Labour of Game Live Streaming', Games and Culture 2021, DOI 10.1177/15554120211005239; 100 interviews with professional and semi-professional streamers over 2 years; qualitative, no income figures; cited here at second hand - the paper itself is paywalled
quoted_support: a recent study titled Behind the Streams: The Off-Camera Labour of Game Live Streaming that based its findings on a 100 interviews with streamers over the course of a 2-year period, time spent behind the scene breaks into four distinct categories.
region: Not stated in the citing source; likely Anglophone Western

claim: Platform holders possess complete information about every creator's earnings while creators possess none about each other's, an asymmetry the 2021 leak temporarily reversed.
stance_target: The scarcity of creator income data is a designed feature of platform labour markets rather than a measurement difficulty
scope_conditions: Analyst argument, not measured; applies to Twitch specifically but generalises across creator platforms
quoted_support: Platform holders hold an advantage over complementors because they know how much everyone else is making and you, as a content creator, do not. But in a single swoop that veil has now been lifted.

claim: A 2020 study of a live streaming platform found a mostly positive causal effect of audience size on tipping revenue under pay-what-you-want pricing, consistent with the power-law revenue curve observed in entertainment generally.
stance_target: Creator income concentration is a predictable consequence of audience-size dynamics rather than an anomaly
scope_conditions: SSRN working paper abstract 3516777, 2020, 'Do Larger Audiences Generate Greater Revenues under Pay What You Want? Evidence from a Live Streaming Platform'; platform and country not stated in the citing source; cited at second hand - direct fetch blocked
quoted_support: showed 'a mostly positive casual effect of audience size on tipping revenues' which is consistent with the power curve we generally see in entertainment.
